title: Adjuvant abemaciclib + endocrine therapy

agents.name: Abemaciclib
agents.explanation: Abemaciclib inhibits CDK4 and CDK6 proteins. These proteins help cells move towards division. It is combined with endocrine treatment to reduce recurrence risk in eligible high-risk early breast cancer.
agents.watch: Start the prescribed diarrhoea rescue plan at the first loose stool and contact the team. Breathlessness, a swollen painful leg, fever or jaundice need prompt assessment.

agents.name: Your endocrine treatment
agents.explanation: The chosen endocrine medicine either reduces oestrogen production or blocks its action. An aromatase inhibitor may need ovarian suppression before menopause. The exact drug and duration are prescribed separately.
agents.watch: Tell the team about joint pain, hot flushes, vaginal symptoms and mood changes. The bone-health and clot-risk discussion depends on the drug chosen.
risks: Hot flushes, joint or muscle symptoms
Bone loss with AI / ovarian suppression
Clot and uterine risks with tamoxifen

context_label: HR-positive / HER2-negative early breast cancer · adjuvant
purpose: For eligible high-risk node-positive early breast cancer, adding abemaciclib to endocrine therapy reduces the risk of recurrence after surgery.
schedule_summary: The usual abemaciclib starting dose is 150 mg twice daily; a lower dose or altered schedule may be prescribed. Abemaciclib is taken twice daily continuously for up to two years with endocrine therapy, unless recurrence or unacceptable toxicity requires an earlier change. A four-week dispensing block is not a rest cycle. Endocrine treatment normally continues beyond abemaciclib.

phases_note: A general pathway, not an appointment calendar. Your team confirms the order, overlap and duration; no date entry is needed.
timeline_note: Treatment bands show the source schedule. Symptom bands show possible patterns, not measured probabilities; serious effects can occur at any time.
safety_note: Fever, shivers or suddenly feeling unwell require immediate contact. Serious symptoms override the timeline or diary.
teachback: Which medicine is taken when, which test is due next, who reviews it, and which symptoms mean you should call today?
consent_support: Discuss the treatment aim, alternatives, benefit and uncertainty, important medicine-specific risks, reproductive precautions, symptom support and planned duration. Confirm the endocrine partner and any ovarian-suppression plan. The timeline does not authorise a restart or certify clinical review.
urgent_extra: Report new breathlessness, chest symptoms, severe diarrhoea, inability to drink, jaundice, a painful swollen leg or a severe rash promptly. You do not need to identify which medicine caused the symptom.

support.title: Diarrhoea rescue from the first loose stool
support.text: Have the prescribed antidiarrhoeal treatment available before starting. Begin the agreed plan at the first loose stool, increase fluids as advised and contact the team early; persistent symptoms or dehydration may require a treatment hold.

support.title: Nausea support
support.text: NCCP classifies abemaciclib as oral moderate–high emetic risk. Agree preventive or rescue antiemetics using individual risk and local oral-SACT policy.

support.title: Blood, liver and symptom checks
support.text: Attend early two-weekly then monthly checks even when tablets are taken at home. Seek prompt advice for infection, jaundice, new breathing symptoms or possible blood clots.

support.title: Endocrine and bone support
support.text: Discuss symptoms and bone protection for the actual endocrine partner. Ovarian suppression is required with an AI before menopause. Endocrine treatment normally continues after the two-year abemaciclib course.

support.title: Medicines and supply
support.text: Take tablets whole at the prescribed regular times. There is no routine week off. Check grapefruit/CYP3A interactions and do not double a missed or vomited dose.

questions.a: The usual abemaciclib starting dose is 150 mg twice daily; a lower dose or altered schedule may be prescribed. Abemaciclib is taken twice daily continuously for up to two years with endocrine therapy, unless recurrence or unacceptable toxicity requires an earlier change. A four-week dispensing block is not a rest cycle. Endocrine treatment normally continues beyond abemaciclib. At completion of the planned two-year abemaciclib course, continue the separately agreed endocrine and follow-up plan.

questions.q: Which checks happen before and during treatment?
questions.a: FBC, renal, liver and bone profile; ECG as clinically indicated. Confirm node-positive high-risk eligibility, definitive surgery and timing: within 16 months of resection and up to 12 weeks of endocrine treatment after the last non-endocrine treatment before starting. Assess VTE history, bowel function, all medicines, endocrine partner, ovarian suppression if using an AI before menopause, and bone/reproductive health. FBC, renal, liver and bone profile every two weeks for the first two months, monthly for the next two months, then as clinically indicated. More frequent liver monitoring for grade 2 or worse liver abnormalities. ECG is driven by clinical need; no routine ribociclib Day-14 ECG schedule. Early and ongoing diarrhoea review, hydration/intake, infection, clots, breathlessness and adherence; prompt action between appointments. Creatinine can rise through inhibited tubular secretion without a true fall in filtration; assess the clinical context and alternative renal measures if needed.

questions.q: Do I need to enter dates?
questions.a: No. This map shows general timing without personal information. Your hospital arranges actual appointments; ask who books each test and who reviews its result.

questions.q: What if a dose is missed or treatment is held?
questions.a: Take abemaciclib twice daily at regular times with or without food. Swallow whole; do not split, chew or crush. Avoid grapefruit. Do not replace a missed or vomited dose. A clinical hold and restart require the treating team’s instructions. A hold may affect one medicine rather than the whole combination; confirm each component.

questions.q: What does the evidence mean for me?
questions.a: Adding a planned course of abemaciclib to endocrine therapy reduced the chance of invasive cancer returning in eligible high-risk, node-positive early breast cancer. Longer follow-up also showed an overall-survival benefit. These group results do not predict your own outcome.

questions.q: What happens after treatment changes or ends?
questions.a: At completion of the planned two-year abemaciclib course, continue the separately agreed endocrine and follow-up plan. Keep the separately agreed disease follow-up, endocrine and bone-health plan.

evidence.title: monarchE: primary OS and seven-year outcomes
evidence.intro: Studies describe groups. Ask how closely the treatment and study population match your situation.
evidence.population: 5,637 patients with HR-positive/HER2-negative, node-positive high-risk early breast cancer; intention-to-treat trial population. NCCP00619 uses its specified clinicopathological high-risk criteria.
evidence.interpretation: Adding a planned course of abemaciclib to endocrine therapy reduced the chance of invasive cancer returning in eligible high-risk, node-positive early breast cancer. Longer follow-up also showed an overall-survival benefit. These group results do not predict your own outcome.
evidence.limitations: Your team can discuss the strength and limitations of the evidence alongside treatment risks and alternatives.

chapters.title: Your treatment aim
chapters.intro: For eligible high-risk node-positive early breast cancer, adding abemaciclib to endocrine therapy reduces the risk of recurrence after surgery.

items.title: Who this treatment is for
items.text: HR-positive/HER2-negative node-positive early breast cancer at high recurrence risk: four or more positive axillary nodes, or one to three with tumour at least 5 cm and/or grade 3. The NCCP timing, prior-treatment and other exclusions remain applicable; this is not a node-negative or metastatic regimen.

sections.title: Before starting
sections.text: Confirm the exact medicine, strength, endocrine partner, baseline tests and first review appointments. Ask who arranges tests and who reviews the results.

sections.title: Taking treatment
sections.text: Take abemaciclib twice daily at regular times with or without food. Swallow whole; do not split, chew or crush. Avoid grapefruit. Do not replace a missed or vomited dose. A clinical hold and restart require the treating team’s instructions.

sections.title: Treatment duration
sections.text: At completion of the planned two-year abemaciclib course, continue the separately agreed endocrine and follow-up plan.

sections.title: Supply and appointments
sections.text: Request the next supply before tablets run out. Blood tests and any ECG or injections need their own appointments. This oral treatment does not itself require a central line or infusion pump.

sections.title: If treatment is held
sections.text: Ask which medicine is held, whether the endocrine partner continues, what needs to recover, when the next review is due and who will authorise restart.

sections.title: Support between appointments
sections.text: Keep the oncology contact details and prescribed symptom medicines accessible. New severe symptoms need prompt assessment rather than waiting for the next blood test.

anatomy: Often starts early. Begin your prescribed diarrhoea plan and contact the team; persistent symptoms may require a treatment hold.
Keep blood tests. Fever, shivers or sudden illness: contact oncology immediately.
Keep liver blood tests. Report jaundice, dark urine or upper-abdominal discomfort promptly.
New cough or breathlessness needs prompt assessment.
A painful swollen leg or new chest / breathing symptoms needs urgent assessment. Severe breathlessness or chest pain: emergency help.
AI and ovarian suppression can thin bones; discuss fracture risk and the monitoring plan.
